title: Bengal raises pay of contractual panchayat staff by Rs 5,000 to Rs 10,000 a month
dek: A Finance Department order backdates the increase to 1 November for contractual workers in the Panchayat and Rural Development Department, but leaves out six categories, including engineers and block-level accounts assistants.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The West Bengal government has raised the monthly pay of contractual employees in its Panchayat and Rural Development Department by between Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000, with effect from 1 November, under an order issued by the state Finance Department on Monday.

The increase is tiered by current pay. Workers earning up to Rs 25,000 a month get Rs 5,000 more, those earning Rs 25,001 to Rs 45,000 get Rs 7,000 more, and those earning above Rs 45,000 get Rs 10,000 more, according to reports of the order. A worker on Rs 20,000 would move to Rs 25,000, one on Rs 30,000 to Rs 37,000 and one on Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000. The order also revises associated benefits.

## Who is left out

Six categories of contractual staff are excluded, according to reports: workers on separate pay structures set under the Finance Department's guidelines of 16 September 2011 and later orders; IT personnel engaged under 2020 guidelines of the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Training and Welfare Department; CHCMI personnel; contractual sub-assistant, junior and assistant engineers; block-level accounts and administrative assistants; and any contractual employee who received a raise in the previous two years.

"The revised rates will be applicable from November 1, subject to the eligibility conditions specified in the notification," a senior official at the state secretariat said, according to reports. The government has not said how many workers will benefit or what the increase will cost.

## Background

Contractual workers do much of the day-to-day work of rural government in Bengal, from data entry and accounts in block offices to running rural employment and housing schemes at gram panchayat level. Unlike permanent government employees, they are not on regular pay scales.

The order is the latest in a series of pay rises for contractual and temporary staff since the BJP government led by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari took office in May. On 7 September the state cabinet approved increases for 14 groups of workers, about one lakh people in all, at an added cost of about Rs 390 crore a year, Adhikari said at the time. They included a Rs 5,000 monthly rise for 20,343 para-teachers and Shiksha Bandhus from 1 November and Rs 5,000 for forest staff from 1 October. Contractual staff of the School Education Department's missions and PM-POSHAN received a pay rise from 1 October.

## What happens next

The revised pay applies from November, subject to each worker meeting the order's conditions. The rise comes ahead of municipal elections in Kolkata and Howrah, which Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said in June would be held by December.
